paper.title: The Wage Effects of Offshoring: Evidence from Danish Matched Worker-Firm Data
paper.code_data_availability: Verbatim (p. 1597, author footnote): 'The data used in our paper is proprietary, and must be physically stored on servers located at Statistics Denmark and may not be transferred to computers outside Statistics Denmark due to data security …

firm balance-sheet variables (output, capital, profits, material purchases)

registers.role: outcomes (hourly wage, labor income, earnings); worker characteristics; skill and occupation

registers.name_in_paper: Firm-Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (FIDA)
registers.role: linkage of workers to firms (week 48 of each year)
treatment: firm-level imports and exports by product and country; pre-sample (1994) shares for the instruments
variables_mentioned: imports by origin country and product
exports by destination country and product
eight-digit Combined Nomenclature aggregated to HS6

registers.role: instrument construction: world export supply (WES) and world import demand (WID) at the HS6 level

registers.name_in_paper: US imports data (for the Hummels 2007 transport cost functions)
registers.role: instrument construction: estimated transport costs by country-product-year
occupational task characteristics (routine, non-routine, social sciences, natural sciences, communication)

linkages: Workers are linked to firms through FIDA, which links every firm in FirmStat with every worker in IDA who is employed by that firm in week 48 of each year, including temporary workers
Product-level trade flows are matched to the worker-firm data annually because the Trade Statistics Register uses the same firm identifier as FirmStat and FIDA
Worker occupations (from IDA) are matched to O*NET task characteristics
The worker identifier in IDA and FIDA is unchanged throughout 1995-2006, which allows workers to be tracked across employers and employment states

sample.universe: The universe of private-sector Danish firms and the population of the Danish labor force, 1995-2006 (IDA covers the entire Danish population aged 15-74); the estimation sample is manufacturing firms and their full-time workers
sample.unit_of_observation: Worker-firm-year for the wage regressions; firm-year for the firm-level regressions; firm-cohort-year for the cohort analysis
selection_rules: Keep manufacturing firms only; drop firms whose classification switches between manufacturing and service industries
Drop worker-firm-year observations if the job spell lasts for a single year
Drop firms with fewer than 50 employees and less than 0.6 million DKK in imports
Include firms only in the years in which they both import and export (required by the IV strategy); a firm's first year of trading is treated as pre-sample
Table 8: drop workers who switch occupations during job spells (except the industry-experience column)
Table 7 panel I: keep only job spells lasting at least seven years
Section VI cohorts: workers aged 20-54 in one of the base years 1995-2001 (reduces the sample by 9.6 percent)
sample.period: 1995-2006 (trade data from 1990; pre-sample instrument weights from 1994; industry affiliations traced back to 1988; cohort base years 1995-2001)
sample.n_observations: About 1.95 million worker-firm-year and 9,800 firm-year observations; the main wage regressions use 1,928,599 worker-firm-year observations in 383,035 job spells

construction_notes: Hourly wage = annual labor income plus mandatory pension fund payments divided by annual hours; full-time workers only
High-skilled = tertiary education in the two highest ISCED categories (5 and 6); all other workers are low-skilled

Narrow offshoring = the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports); it captures 70.8 percent of a firm's imports. Broad offshoring = total imports of the firm

Trade flows are aggregated from the eight-digit Combined Nomenclature to roughly 5,000 HS6 products for compatibility with COMTRADE; the data account for 90-95 percent of official Danish imports in every year

Instruments: I_jt = sum over country c and product k of s_jck * I_ckt, where s_jck is the firm's pre-sample (1994) share of c-k in total materials imports (or exports) and I_ckt is world export supply, world import demand, or estimated transport costs; for firms that start offshoring in sample the first year of offshoring is used as the pre-sample

Transport costs are built by estimating cost functions on US imports data following Hummels (2007) and applying them to pre-sample destination, bulk and modal information; the key variation is distance x modal use x oil prices
Trade variables enter the wage regressions as levels of logs, deliberately not scaled by firm size, so that trade-induced changes in firm size are not differenced away

Task characteristics are principal components of O*NET characteristics, normalized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1; industry-specific experience is years in the 2-digit NACE industry between 1988 and the start of the job spell, fixed within the spell

Cohort analysis: for each firm and base year v (1995-2001) two cohorts (all high-skilled and all low-skilled workers employed there in v), 9,000 cohorts in total, tracked for t = v+1,...,v+5; outcomes are changes in cohort averages relative to the base year; hourly wages and earnings of non-employed members are set to zero, as are outcomes in the 0.8 percent of observations with exits (death or emigration)
Gross earnings = earnings plus unemployment insurance benefits plus social assistance

The five-year PDV in Table 10 is the discounted sum of the five yearly coefficients at a 4 percent discount rate, with delta-method standard errors; the cohort regressions are weighted by base-year cohort size

claims.statement: An exogenous increase in the log of the employing firm's narrow offshoring changes the log hourly wage of low-skilled workers within job spells (Table 5, column 1, FE).

register_source.value: Danish Foreign Trade Statistics Register: firm-level imports by origin country and HS6 product (aggregated from eight-digit Combined Nomenclature); no DST variable names are given

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Enters the wage equation as the level of the log, deliberately not scaled by firm size. Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares.

timing.value: Year t, contemporaneous with the outcome

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), matched to firms through FIDA; no DST variable names are given

definition.value: Log of the hourly wage rate of worker i in firm j in year t, measured as annual labor income plus mandatory pension fund payments divided by annual hours; full-time workers only.

timing.value: Year t, within the worker-firm job spell

units.value: elasticity: log change in the outcome per log change in the firm's narrow offshoring (the low-skilled elasticity, S_i = 0)

estimand.target_population: Low-skilled (non-tertiary) full-time workers staying in manufacturing firms that both import and export
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: the wage in year t is related to the employing firm's offshoring and exports in year t, within the job spell

population.description: Full-time workers in Danish manufacturing firms with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, in the years in which the firm both imports and exports, 1995-2006; only workers staying in the firm (job spells lasting more than one year).
population.selection: Worker-firm-year observations are kept only if the job spell lasts more than one year, the firm is a manufacturing firm with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, and the firm both imports and exports in that year; a firm's first year of trading is treated as pre-sample. Identification is within job spells, i.e. conditional on the worker remaining with the firm.

identification.source_of_variation: Within-job-spell, over-time variation in the employing firm's narrow offshoring and exports, with no instrumenting

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on job-spell, industry-year and regional fixed effects (plus worker and firm controls), within-job-spell changes in the firm's offshoring and exports are uncorrelated with the wage residual. The authors state that this specification ignores the simultaneity problem and that the FE-IV specification is the one that corrects it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors reject it: the FE columns 'ignore the potential simultaneity problem where unobserved firm productivities drive both wages and offshoring', and the IV estimates are roughly ten times larger

rhs: unobserved determinants of log hourly wage
given: firm controls (columns with firm controls only)

implies_edges.from: time-varying firm productivity and output-demand shocks (A_jt, psi_jt)

key_assumptions.assumption: Worker mobility is random conditional on job-spell fixed effects (and other observable worker and firm controls).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 9; the cohort analysis of Section VI

implies_edges.from: remaining in the same job spell (sample inclusion)

threats_discussed: Firm-level shocks to demand or productivity drive both trade and wage setting (simultaneity bias)
World export supply may reflect world-wide (and Danish) demand shocks, not only supply shocks
Oil-price variation in the transport-cost instrument may affect the macroeconomy and labor demand
Changes over time in firms' technology could affect both input use and wages (addressed with pre-sample input shares)
Shocks originating with Danish firms could affect prices and volumes in partner markets (small-country argument)
Correlated domestic and foreign demand shocks are a greater concern for the export instruments than for the offshoring instruments
Selection: worker mobility in response to offshoring shocks (Table 9 and the cohort analysis of Section VI)
robustness_checks: Job spells lasting at least seven years (Table 7, panel I)
Restricting to Danish trade with high-income partner countries (Table 7, panel II)
Replacing the WES/WID instruments with their 3-year moving averages, following Bertrand (2004) (Table 7, panel III)
Dropping industries that include computers, steel, flat glass and cement, following Autor, Dorn, and Hanson (2013) (Table 7, panel IV)

Footnote 34 (online appendix): splitting low-skilled into medium-skilled and very low-skilled; top-two or top-five pre-sample trade flows; job spells longer than five years; HS2-based narrow offshoring; broad instead of narrow offshoring; dropping c-k-t flows where Denmark exceeds 1, 10 or 25 percent of trade; adding Danish trade to WES and WID
Footnote 10 (online appendix): balanced panel of firms with positive imports and exports in all years; including firms that offshore but do not export
Dropping c-k-t trade flows where Denmark has a greater than 1 percent share (online appendix)
Instruments entered by themselves and by subgroups in the first stage (footnote 30)
unresolved_confounders: Demand shocks not completely purged from the estimation; the authors argue these would bias the results against finding negative wage effects of offshoring (footnote 28)
The case for identifying the causal effects of exports on wages is weaker than for offshoring, so the export estimates 'merit more caution in interpretation'
Selection on unobservables among the workers who stay in the job spell, which Table 9 cannot address and which motivates the cohort analysis of Section VI

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Enters the wage equation as the level of the log, deliberately not scaled by firm size. This regressor is the interaction with S_i, a dummy equal to 1 if worker i has a tertiary education corresponding to the two highest ISCED categories (5 and 6), 0 otherwise; its coefficient is the differential offshoring wage elasticity of high-skilled relative to low-skilled workers, so the high-skilled elasticity is b_L,M + b_M1. claims.statement: An exogenous increase in the log of the employing firm's narrow offshoring changes the log hourly wage of low-skilled workers within job spells (Table 5, column 4, FE-IV).

register_source.value: Danish Foreign Trade Statistics Register: firm-level imports by origin country and HS6 product (aggregated from eight-digit Combined Nomenclature); no DST variable names are given

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Enters the wage equation as the level of the log, deliberately not scaled by firm size. Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares.

timing.value: Year t, contemporaneous with the outcome

definition.value: Log of the hourly wage rate of worker i in firm j in year t, measured as annual labor income plus mandatory pension fund payments divided by annual hours; full-time workers only.

timing.value: Year t, within the worker-firm job spell

units.value: elasticity: log change in the outcome per log change in the firm's narrow offshoring (the low-skilled elasticity, S_i = 0)

estimand.target_population: Low-skilled (non-tertiary) full-time workers staying in manufacturing firms that both import and export
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: the wage in year t is related to the employing firm's offshoring and exports in year t, within the job spell

population.description: Full-time workers in Danish manufacturing firms with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, in the years in which the firm both imports and exports, 1995-2006; only workers staying in the firm (job spells lasting more than one year).
population.selection: Worker-firm-year observations are kept only if the job spell lasts more than one year, the firm is a manufacturing firm with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, and the firm both imports and exports in that year; a firm's first year of trading is treated as pre-sample. Identification is within job spells, i.e. conditional on the worker remaining with the firm.

identification.source_of_variation: Within-job-spell, over-time variation in the employing firm's imports and exports driven by country x product x year shocks external to Denmark: world export supply (WES), world import demand (WID) and estimated transport costs, aggregated to the firm with pre-sample (1994) country-product trade shares.
identification.instrument: Firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply, log world import demand and log transport costs (for imports and for exports), weights = firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import/export shares; each also interacted with the high-skill dummy, following Wooldridge (2002).

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Enters the wage equation as the level of the log, deliberately not scaled by firm size. Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares. This regressor is the interaction with S_i, a dummy equal to 1 if worker i has a tertiary education corresponding to the two highest ISCED categories (5 and 6), 0 otherwise; its coefficient is the differential offshoring wage elasticity of high-skilled relative to low-skilled workers, so the high-skilled elasticity is b_L,M + b_M1. The interaction is instrumented by the interactions between high skill and the offshoring instruments, following Wooldridge (2002).

claims.statement: An exogenous increase in the log of the employing firm's narrow offshoring changes the log labor income of low-skilled workers within job spells (Table 5, column 6, FE-IV).

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares.

timing.value: Year t, contemporaneous with the outcome

population.description: Full-time workers in Danish manufacturing firms with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, in the years in which the firm both imports and exports, 1995-2006; only workers staying in the firm (job spells lasting more than one year).

definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares. definition.value: Log of firm j's narrow offshoring in year t: the sum of the firm's imports in the same HS4 category as goods sold by the firm (domestically or in exports). Enters the wage equation as the level of the log, deliberately not scaled by firm size. Instrumented by firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply (WES) and log transport costs, the weights being the firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import shares. This regressor is the interaction with S_i, a dummy equal to 1 if worker i has a tertiary education corresponding to the two highest ISCED categories (5 and 6), 0 otherwise; its coefficient is the differential offshoring wage elasticity of high-skilled relative to low-skilled workers, so the high-skilled elasticity is b_L,M + b_M1. The interaction is instrumented by the interactions between high skill and the offshoring instruments, following Wooldridge (2002).

timing.value: Firm offshoring in year t, contemporaneous with the wage observation, within the worker-firm job spell

definition.value: Log of the hourly wage rate of worker i in firm j in year t, measured as annual labor income plus mandatory pension fund payments divided by annual hours; full-time workers only.

population.selection: Worker-firm-year observations are kept only if the job spell lasts more than one year, the firm is a manufacturing firm with at least 50 employees and at least 0.6 million DKK in imports, and the firm both imports and exports in that year; a firm's first year of trading is treated as pre-sample. Identification is within job spells, i.e. conditional on the worker remaining with the firm.

identification.instrument: Firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply, log world import demand and log transport costs (for imports and for exports), weights = firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import/export shares; each also interacted with the high-skill dummy, following Wooldridge (2002).

Oil-price variation in the transport-cost instrument may affect the macroeconomy and labor demand

definition.value: The cohort's offshoring shock: Delta log OFF_jv+1 = log(OFF_jv+1 / OFF_jv), the percentage change in the PREDICTED narrow offshoring of firm j between the base year v and v+1, a continuous variable. timing.value: Between base year v and v+1 (v = 1995-2001); outcomes tracked for t = v+1,...,v+5

outcome.label: Change in log cohort-average earnings relative to the base year

definition.value: Change in the cohort-average annual earnings relative to the base year, in logs; the earnings of non-employed cohort members are set to zero. Averaged over the cohort of all high-skilled workers employed by firm j in base year v.

timing.value: Year v+2, measured as the change relative to the base year v

units.value: elasticity: log change in the cohort-average outcome relative to the base year per log change in the firm's predicted offshoring (a doubling of offshoring corresponds to a change of 1 in log terms, which is how the paper reads these coefficients as percentages)

estimand.target_population: All high-skilled workers (stayers and leavers) employed by the firm in the base year
estimand.time_horizon: one year after the offshoring shock (delta_2)

population.description: Cohorts of all high-skilled workers employed by a sample manufacturing firm in a base year v (v = 1995-2001), aged 20-54 in one of the base years, tracked for five years; 9,000 such cohorts in total.
population.ages: 20-54 in one of the base years
population.selection: Cohort membership is fixed by employment at firm j in base year v, before the offshoring shock; workers aged 20-54 in one of the base years (this drops 9.6 percent of the sample); in the 0.8 percent of observations with exits (death or emigration) outcomes are set to zero

identification.source_of_variation: The change in PREDICTED firm-level offshoring between the base year and the following year, built from the first-stage IV regressions of Section IV (world export supply, world import demand and transport costs weighted by pre-sample country-product trade shares), for cohorts fixed before the shock

claims.statement: The overall effect of an exogenous offshoring shock on the change in log cohort-average earnings of low-skilled first-year leavers cohorts, the year of the offshoring shock (the contemporaneous effect, delta_1) (Table 10, column 8).

treatment.label: Offs. shock (change in log predicted offshoring of the firm between the base year and the following year)

register_source.value: Danish Foreign Trade Statistics Register: firm-level imports by origin country and HS6 product (aggregated from eight-digit Combined Nomenclature); no DST variable names are given

definition.value: The cohort's offshoring shock: Delta log OFF_jv+1 = log(OFF_jv+1 / OFF_jv), the percentage change in the PREDICTED narrow offshoring of firm j between the base year v and v+1, a continuous variable. Predicted values come from the first-stage IV regressions of Section IV, so that the shocks are exogenous to the firms and workers.

timing.value: Between base year v and v+1 (v = 1995-2001); outcomes tracked for t = v+1,...,v+5

outcome.label: Change in log average earnings relative to the base year (first-year leavers)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), matched to firms through FIDA; no DST variable names are given

definition.value: Change in the cohort-average annual earnings relative to the base year, in logs; the earnings of non-employed cohort members are set to zero. Averaged over the first-year leavers: the cohort members who are no longer employed by the firm in the year after the base year.

timing.value: Year v+1, measured as the change relative to the base year v

units.value: elasticity: log change in the cohort-average outcome relative to the base year per log change in the firm's predicted offshoring (a doubling of offshoring corresponds to a change of 1 in log terms, which is how the paper reads these coefficients as percentages)

estimand.target_population: The low-skilled workers who leave the firm in the year after the base year
estimand.time_horizon: the year of the offshoring shock (the contemporaneous effect, delta_1)

population.description: Cohorts of all low-skilled workers employed by a sample manufacturing firm in a base year v (v = 1995-2001), aged 20-54 in one of the base years, tracked for five years; 9,000 such cohorts in total, restricted here to the first-year leavers.
population.ages: 20-54 in one of the base years
population.selection: Cohort membership is fixed by employment at firm j in base year v, before the offshoring shock; workers aged 20-54 in one of the base years (this drops 9.6 percent of the sample); in the 0.8 percent of observations with exits (death or emigration) outcomes are set to zero

identification.source_of_variation: The change in PREDICTED firm-level offshoring between the base year and the following year, built from the first-stage IV regressions of Section IV (world export supply, world import demand and transport costs weighted by pre-sample country-product trade shares), for cohorts fixed before the shock
identification.instrument: Firm-level weighted averages of log world export supply, log world import demand and log transport costs (for imports and for exports), weights = firm's pre-sample (1994) country-product import/export shares; each also interacted with the high-skill dummy, following Wooldridge (2002).
